s1.syndrome_frame: Widespread skin condition with progressive worsening and characteristic plaques
salient_findings: Widespread polycyclic serpiginous, erythematous plaques with a double-edged scale
key_facts: The patient is a 32-year-old woman
The skin condition has progressively worsened
The condition involves 90% of her body surface area
There are widespread polycyclic serpiginous, erythematous plaques on the trunk and extremities
The plaques involve 30% of the body surface area
The patient has sparse and short eyebrow hairs
The patient has coarse and brittle scalp hairs
Skin biopsy showed psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia with spongiosis
Trichography showed nodal swelling, with invagination of the distal hair into the proximal end

shortlist.label: Pityriasis rubra pilaris
shortlist.why_kept: Characteristic psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia and widespread erythematous plaques

shortlist.label: Psoriasis vulgaris
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia and erythematous plaques

raw.rationale: The patient's skin condition involves a large body surface area, with characteristic polycyclic serpiginous erythematous plaques and double-edged scale, along with sparse and short eyebrow hairs and coarse brittle scalp hairs, which are consistent with the clinical features of Pityriasis rubra pilaris. The skin biopsy showing psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia with spongiosis and trichography findings of nodal swelling also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Psoriasis vulgaris
rejected.why: While the skin biopsy shows psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia, the clinical presentation and trichography findings are more consistent with Pityriasis rubra pilaris

rejected.label: Erythroderma
rejected.why: Erythroderma is a more generalized condition, but the specific findings of polycyclic serpiginous plaques and hair abnormalities point more towards Pityriasis rubra pilaris

rejected.label: Dermatomyositis
rejected.why: Dermatomyositis typically presents with muscle weakness and specific skin findings such as Gottron's papules, which are not mentioned in the case

rejected.label: Ichthyosis vulgaris
rejected.why: Ichthyosis vulgaris is a condition of dry, scaly skin, but it does not typically present with the acute onset and specific plaques seen in this patient

rejected.label: Keratosis pilaris
rejected.why: Keratosis pilaris is a condition of small, rough patches on the skin, but it does not match the widespread and severe presentation of this patient's condition

rejected.label: Parapsoriasis
rejected.why: Parapsoriasis is a group of conditions that can present with varied skin findings, but the specific features of this patient's condition are more consistent with Pityriasis rubra pilaris

rejected.label: Seborrheic dermatitis
rejected.why: Seborrheic dermatitis typically presents with a more localized distribution, often involving the scalp, face, and torso, and does not match the widespread and severe presentation of this patient's condition
